question.text: The number of one-one functions <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>:</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>→</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>a</mi></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>b</mi></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>d</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> is _____

solution.text:
Given 2fa+3 fc=fb-fd

Using fundamental principle of counting,

when fc=0, fa=1 then  fb-fd=2 has 7 choices,

Similarly when fc=0, fa=2 then fb-fd has 5 choices.

Counting like this we get the total number of one-one function as 31
